source.title: EraseSAE: Surgical Concept Erasure in Text-to-Video Diffusion Models via Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Xing-Hao Wang; Dong Li; Wei Yu; Ying-Wei Pan; Tao Gong; Qi Chu; Neng-Hai Yu; Ting Yao

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests semantic purity of SAE features in text-to-video diffusion models, a setting distinct from the LLM feature claims; it does not test the original toy-model superposition setup.
record.gate_note: Included the paper's measurements of feature purity and cross-identity selectivity. Erasure benchmark scores and SAE-architecture comparisons report erasure performance, not superposition geometry or whether SAE features are complete, stable canonical units, so they are not rows. Results cited from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: This is a concept-erasure methods paper. It trains a supervised, partitioned convolutional SAE whose concept kernels are made concept-specific by design: per-concept channel partitions, a leakage penalty and cross-attention mask supervision. It then selects kernels by contrastive attribution and reports how well its own method performs. The purity and selectivity numbers describe its engineered, selected kernels against a linear SAE. They do not test whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units (V5), and no version's claim about superposition is measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that EraseSAE, via PConvSAE decomposition and contrastive attribution, achieves state-of-the-art concept erasure in T2V models with minimal quality loss, by intervening on 'monosemantic' features rather than polysemantic neurons. Monosemanticity is asserted and supported only by purity and heatmap checks on their own trained kernels.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains a partitioned convolutional SAE on spatiotemporal activations from diffusion models and uses its kernels for concept erasure; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method.

fits_no_version.finding: In DiT video diffusion activations, kernels attributed to 5 celebrity identities have mean class purity of 0.76 for the supervised PConvSAE and 0.37 for a linear SAE (Sec. 4.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Supervised, partitioned SAEs can produce more class-pure concept features than standard linear SAEs in video diffusion models, though this purity is engineered by training losses.

record.problems: The feature-purity analysis covers five celebrity identities and reports no uncertainty estimates. The text does not identify the model used for the purity/heatmap results. Purity and cross-identity selectivity do not establish feature completeness, stability, canonicality, or superposition geometry.
record.rows_left_out: Erasure benchmark outcomes and ablation results were left out because they measure erasure efficacy or generation quality rather than the representation claims. See Tables 1–6 and Sections 4.1–4.3.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transitions or geometry.
No capacity competition or dedicated-vs-shared dimension analysis.
No analysis of the causes of polysemantic neurons; polysemanticity is only asserted in the introduction.
No LLMs. Only diffusion transformers are studied, and no unsupervised feature-recovery quality is measured.
Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicality are not measured. The purity of supervised, selected kernels is by design.

record.verdict_notes: The record's peer_reviewed field ('European Conference on Computer Vision') is not supported by the text, which shows only an arXiv v2 header. The models are CogVideoX-5B, HunyuanVideo and Flux.1 [dev], but the text does not say which model the purity and heatmap results use. Erasure tables were rightly excluded as method performance.

versions.untested_parts: No test of overcomplete sparse features, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometric structure in toy networks.
No test of capacity competition, dedicated versus shared dimensions, or neuron polysemanticity as a capacity effect.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
The tested systems are text-to-video diffusion models, not LLMs; no LLM feature distribution or recovery is measured.
Measures semantic purity/selectivity of selected SAE kernels, but does not establish that SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model's representation.
No test of whether represented features are one-dimensional directions versus multidimensional features; the architecture comparison measures erasure outcomes, not feature geometry.

rows.subject: PConvSAE concept kernels (model not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Measured semantic purity of locked feature kernels across celebrity classes.
rows.measure: Mean class purity of locked kernels
rows.note: The paper says the value is averaged over the 5 identities and describes it as evidence of high monosemanticity. This measures purity, not completeness, stability, or canonicality.
rows.check: This is the study's own method compared with a baseline. The kernels are selected by contrastive attribution and trained with a leakage penalty built to enforce purity, so high purity is induced by design. Purity on 5 identities says nothing about completeness, stability or canonicality. The diffusion model used for this measurement is not stated.

rows.subject: Linear SAE (model not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Measured semantic purity of locked feature kernels for comparison with PConvSAE.
rows.measure: Mean class purity of locked kernels
rows.note: The paper reports this as less than half the PConvSAE purity; this is a comparison of feature purity, not a test of whether SAE features are complete, stable canonical units.
rows.check: This is a comparator value for the method comparison, not a test of V5. The state 'partial' is meaningless here, since the row measures purity of selected kernels, not the V5 properties. The model is not stated.

rows.subject: PConvSAE target concept kernels (model not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Compared kernel activation magnitudes across prompts for five celebrity identities.

conditions.value: Donald Trump, Barack Obama, Elon Musk, Queen Elizabeth, Taylor Swift

rows.value: The heatmap is described as showing strong diagonal dominance and minimal cross-activation to other identities.
rows.note: The paper describes the qualitative pattern, but the text extraction does not support reliable assignment of the individual heatmap numbers to identity pairs. This supports selectivity, not completeness or stability.
rows.check: This is a qualitative heatmap of the method's own concept-partitioned kernels, whose diagonal dominance is enforced by training (partitioning plus L_leak). It is not a test of the claim. Extracted heatmap values are garbled: the figure seems to include method rows (Original, Neg Prompt, SAFREE, Ours), so the assignment of values is unclear.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: PConvSAE kernels for the five tested celebrity identities
reader_labels.reason: The reported purity (r1) and cross-identity selectivity (r3) support semantic specificity in this tested setting; they do not establish completeness, stability, or canonicality.
